report.title: Edition 2, Chapter 18 — Giving the Agent the Web, and a Status Line

checks.title: The web tools are absent until the web-search skill is loaded. Off is a statement about what this feature initiates, and the honest way to show it is that there is no tool to call.
A skill declaring transport: url reaches a hosted MCP server and its tools appear in the list sent to the model. This is the seam Chapter 12 left open, filled in.
A search call reaches the server and its results come back to the model as a tool result, rather than being dispatched and dropped.
Content fetched from a page arrives at the model intact. Verified with a token minted this run, so a stub or a cached fixture cannot produce it.

Fetched bytes stay inside a tool result and never reach the system prompt or a user turn. Web pages contain instructions aimed at the model; keeping them structurally separate from the operator's words is what makes them data.
A tool-level failure (isError on a 200) is told to the model. A failure the model cannot see is one it will confidently narrate around.

An HTTP-level failure reaches the model with the reason intact. The response body is where quota and auth refusals say what went wrong; a transport that discards it turns a diagnosable refusal into 'request failed'.
Actual core and GUI commands build
Shipped agent_status: actual model, four last/session counts and cache hit rate
Priced work and honest mixed-model accounting across turn-boundary switches
Resolved tools/common import boundary; ownership requires source review
details: Mandatory source review follows actual dispatched status → owning Engine → Agent → Ensemble and each shipped executable's public composition path; this graph alone proves neither.

checks.title: A spawned child runs and reports back: the parent calls spawn_sub_agent and the child's submitted payload reaches the parent
Parent and two children retain distinct valid saved conversations
Fleet visibility and teardown: agents_status lists a live child, and shutdown_agent removes it
join_agents blocks until every listed child finishes, then returns each child's result
Three generations yield a child question and return an addressed parent reply
A message arriving during a slow tool wakes the agent before that tool finishes, and the backgrounded tool's result still arrives
A child that goes idle without submitting is woken rather than treated as finished, and after three wakes it escalates to its parent
Correlated activity and validated structured submission state
Named creation selects model/skill, restores conversation and deletes durably
Owned typed retrieval and indistinguishable foreign/missing refusal
Selected child progress wakes its change wait; command and submission complete
Actual CLI recursively constructs and completes a three-generation fleet
Live nested GUI tree, exact structured replay and truthful state
Bottom-up submit and idle correction still work through the Ensemble layer
A checkpoint that crosses the budget turns the oldest finished work into a memory, and the raw work it replaces leaves the context.
The compressor is shown the work it is folding, and what it writes comes back as context.
A band over its budget folds its OLDEST contents into the band above, leaving the newest alone.
Switching bands off and back on - in any order - restores exactly the memory that was there before.
A band whose upper neighbour is switched off refuses to graduate rather than dropping memories on the floor.
A nearly full context leaves micro_handoff as the only tool on offer, because asking nicely does not work.
Rebuilding a context replays recorded decisions instead of re-running the model that made them.
A fold that fails or is interrupted loses no work and is never applied twice.
Memory arrives in the conversation, written in the first person, not bolted onto the system prompt.
An agent starting with memory files on disk comes up with them already in context.
Chapter 14 context management and journaling remain functional.
Archived text the user never mentioned reaches the model, so the archive is actually indexed and searched.
Results are ranked by term rarity, term frequency and document length, not merely by containing the word.
Words like "the" and "we" are stripped, so a short document full of them cannot outrank a real match.
A long document is indexed section by section, so retrieving one part does not cost the context of the whole file.
Each source keeps a share of the result, so the source with the most text on a topic cannot take every slot.
A model reads the candidates and its verdict decides what is attached; changing its answer changes the output.
Prose, HTTP 500, a hang, and an empty archive all degrade to top-N BM25 or to silence. Never a crash, never a dead turn.
internal/recall imports the hub and stdlib only, and no existing spoke imports it back.
Recalled material lands as its own permanent entry carrying its bytes, and is never merged into the user's message.
The attached block is bounded, so an archive that matches well everywhere cannot swallow the context window.
Noise-KK handshake: two peers mutually authenticate, wrong keys are rejected
Prompt envelope carries provenance, trust, conversation and response mode
Actual Gateway binary: authenticated identities and welcome queue counts
Group-based routing delivers only from accepted groups and rejects the rest
Handler-return receipt, ordered offline/resume and clean server restart
Actual outside Client/Handler and resolved public dependency boundary
Parent registers a child and cannot grant groups it does not hold
